clue.text: Start to learn about Tibet suppressing resistance, before one books

indicators.note: the start of the word learn supplies just its opening letter
Tibet suppresses, i.e. holds down within it, the letter for resistance
about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone begins studying Tibet, with talk of suppressing resistance there, before reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' puts R inside TIBET, and 'about' then rearranges those six letters into IBRETT, between L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The texts of operas are each called a libretto, literally a little book, so the plural is a fair synonym for books.

clue.text: See 25
Drink 'turned on' hotel employee

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

indicators.note: the word on, given as a synonym, is turned to run backwards

parts.note: RE means on, concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A hotel worker who has had a drink becomes switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes mark 'turned on' as a unit: on gives RE, and turned makes it ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter carries luggage and attends the door in a hotel, so it names a staff member there.

clue.text: Penny fills black pudding, which emits gases

parts.note: jet is a deep black stone, hence jet black

indicators.note: the penny goes into the pudding, filling it

parts.note: a pie is a baked savoury or sweet dish, a pudding in the broad British sense
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A coin is stuffed into a black pudding, which then gives off wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Black pudding is a British blood sausage, but here black and pudding are separate pieces. The definition stands for 'something which emits gases'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet engine's exhaust duct carries the hot exhaust out, so it is the part that sends gases out.

clue.text: See 26 across
It could denote feet of little note

parts.note: minute means tiny
a mark is a note or sign made on something

explanation.surface: A musical query: what symbol might show the feet of a short note?
explanation.walkthrough: Feet of a note sounds musical or metrical, but the prime symbol ′ is used to mark feet in measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime symbol used for minutes of arc also stands for feet in imperial measurements, as in 6′ for six feet.

clue.text: As it was written round the loo of a certain European?

indicators.note: the word sic goes round the toilet, enclosing it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to show a quotation is copied exactly as written
lav is short for lavatory, a British word for the loo

explanation.surface: Graffiti scrawled round a toilet belonging to some European visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is broad: many Europeans are not of this group.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Slav peoples of eastern and central Europe, such as Poles, Czechs and Russians.

clue.text: One in favour of donning long protective wear

indicators.note: pine puts on, or wears, the other letters inside itself

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
for means supporting or in favour of

explanation.surface: A supporter puts on a long protective garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' reads as describing the wear but is the verb yearn. HMS Pinafore is one of several Gilbert and Sullivan operas in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or sleeveless overdress worn to keep clothes clean beneath it.

clue.text: Industrialised housing experiment

indicators.note: the long word Industrialised houses, or contains, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A housing project on an industrial scale is being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote Trial by Jury.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test run of something new, which is what an experiment is.

clue.text: Because there's no beginning a Latin exam

indicators.note: the synonym of because loses its first letter

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

explanation.surface: A Latin exam with no clear starting point.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, such as a viva or language speaking test, is called an oral.

clue.text: In confusion, turn over before syrupy TV broadcast

parts.note: TO is short for turn over, as in PTO, please turn over

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone switches off rather than watch a sugary television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy-Turvy is also Mike Leigh's film about Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topsy-turvy is upside down or in a muddle, which is a state of disorder.

clue.text: Rubbish Proust — result of too much drink?

indicators.note: rubbish here means mess up, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dismissal of Proust's novel as only the product of a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that drink is only one cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, near-unconscious state, which heavy drinking can bring on.

clue.text: Being stoned, has applied a decorative coating

parts.note: pebbled means covered with small stones

indicators.note: applied suggests these letters are reworked, put to a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who is high on drugs has decorated a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests intoxication, but it means set with stones.
explanation.definitionFit: This exterior wall finish is mortar with small stones thrown on, a rough decorative render.

clue.text: Broadcast people treated as a game

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: patients are people receiving medical treatment

explanation.surface: Radio listeners are treated to a game show.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is also a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the British name for solitaire, a card game for one player.

clue.text: New Zealand bird's partial intuition

indicators.note: only part of the word intuition is used

explanation.surface: A bird from New Zealand shows a flicker of intuition.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a honeyeater native to New Zealand, known for its white throat tuft.

clue.text: Mr White's gerbil smeared over Tarantino's head?

indicators.note: smeared means messed up, so the letters are jumbled
the head of the name Tarantino is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pet rodent owned by someone named White is daubed over the film director's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr White recalls the Reservoir Dogs character, but it means Gilbert White, the 18th-century naturalist of Selborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The English naturalist Gilbert White wrote The Natural History of Selborne, so his first name identifies him.

clue.text: On very short cycle

parts.note: RE means on or concerning
V is the abbreviation for very; the letters of very read backwards containing the answer is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A brief bike ride when it is very short.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev is short for revolution, one turn of an engine, and a single revolution is a cycle.

clue.text: Draws breath, since fleeing raiders

indicators.note: the word for since flees, leaving the rest

parts.note: to aspirate is to breathe in
as means since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: Someone gasps for air while running from raiders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are sea robbers who attack and plunder ships, so they are raiders.

clue.text: Poorly experienced Rex turned out to be the ultimate jigsaw puzzle completer

indicators.note: poorly means badly, so the letters are jumbled
Rex is turned out, expelled from the jumble

explanation.surface: An inexperienced king, Rex, is kicked out after failing at a jigsaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Poorly rearranges EXPERIENCED; 'turned out' removes R, E and X from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The last piece placed in a jigsaw finishes it, a playful sense of the term for a final piece or part.

clue.text: Shrunk, emptied — essentially neglected

indicators.note: essentially here means at the core, so the letters come from inside the two words

explanation.surface: Clothes that have shrunk and been emptied out are, at heart, neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt describes untidy, uncared-for hair or appearance, things left uncared for.

clue.text: Celebrated prizefighter making audible smear on vehicle

indicators.note: the synonym for smear is heard, giving a sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to sully is to stain or tarnish
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A famous boxer is caught on camera smearing a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: John L. Sullivan was a famous 19th-century American heavyweight champion; the name also completes Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: John L. Sullivan, the Boston Strong Boy, was the first heavyweight boxing champion under gloves.

clue.text: Ideal place for patio conversion, after you texted

indicators.note: the rearranged patio comes after the letter for you

parts.note: U is text-message shorthand for you

indicators.note: a conversion changes the patio, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Someone's dream of a converted patio, which they told you about by text.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More named an imaginary perfect island Utopia, now any perfect society or place.

clue.text: Emperor king gets in amid dodgy circle

indicators.note: the king gets in among the jumbled letters
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A monarch infiltrates a shady circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado was the title used in the West for the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Somewhat squeamish nanny's contribution to the Talmud

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A rather squeamish nanny adds her bit to Jewish scripture study.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mishna is the written collection of Jewish oral law that forms the first part of the Talmud.

clue.text: Canal workers, for whom there's no hope, welcoming lido refurbishment

indicators.note: the hopeless ones welcome the rearranged letters into their midst

parts.note: goners are people who are doomed

indicators.note: a refurbishment remakes the lido, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Hopeless Venetian boatmen welcome the renovation of a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an open-air public pool. The Gondoliers is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Gondoliers row the boats on the waterways of Venice, so they work the canals.

clue.text: Court judgement row over name

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a line is a row of people or things
to call is to name, as in 'they called him Jack'

explanation.surface: A dispute in court over someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, an umpire's ruling on whether a ball landed in or out is this decision.

clue.text: Water distribution network connected to river support

parts.note: the mains are the supply pipes for water
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A water main is linked up to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support, originally the stay rope holding a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Possible castle fortification said to be minor blemish

indicators.note: said signals the synonym is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a mote is a tiny speck, as in the mote in your eye

explanation.surface: A castle's defences called a mere flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled ditch round a castle is its classic defensive feature, hence possible fortification.

clue.text: From the same source, money makes the writer

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, marks a citation from the same source
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: An author whose earnings come from one source.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Town in New Zealand, one flooded with cash

indicators.note: the letters for New Zealand and one are flooded, surrounded, by the cash

parts.note: pence are small coins, cash
A means one

explanation.surface: A New Zealand town awash with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is in Cornwall, not New Zealand; 'in' is just a link. It is the setting of The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: Penzance is a Cornish port town in the far south-west of England.
